alex: hey 👋 I'm Alex, first day here — quick Q: where should I post hardware/badge questions vs infra/access requests? also curious which bots I should subscribe to as a new hire

sam: welcome Alex! :wave: Hardware & badge stuff goes in #people-ops. For Okta/AWS creds or VPN, use #help (file a short ticket there). Join #new-hires (you are), #devex, and #general. Opt into onboarding bots but mute noisy ones.

tara: hi Alex — for laptop image/replacement open a ticket in #help with "hardware" tag. For repo access or AWS roles, ping #eng-infra or DM @infra-lead. To subscribe to the onboarding checklist run `/onboard subscribe` in a DM with onboarding-bot.

onboarding-bot: Reminder: run `onboard checklist` to get links to VPN, Okta, repo access, and the buddy program. You can also run `onboard links` to pin them. :robot_face:

devin: etiquette note — prefer threads for follow-ups so channels don't get noisy. If it's infra/credentials-related, don't paste anything in Slack (even partial). Use the ticketing flow. Use reactions for ack instead of replies for short confirms.

jess: if you want help with Slack prefs, channel discovery, or muting bots, ping me. Pro tip: star the channels you need, and pin any onboarding docs you reference often.

alex: thanks! one more — where do I request dev API keys for the hosted API? don't want to expose keys in slack.

sam: never post secrets in Slack. For dev keys use the dev portal (link is in the onboarding checklist) or request via #security with the template. If it's urgent, DM @security and add the ticket link.

mike: also, subscribe to deploy-bot only if you're on call or actively deploying; otherwise mute it. You can mute any bot per-channel in channel settings.

tara: small workflow tip — when asking a question that affects multiple teams, start in the relevant channel and @ the team (e.g., @eng-infra). For 1:1 help use threads or DMs. The buddy assigned to you should be your first stop for small Qs.

alex: super helpful — appreciate the quick tour :thumbsup:
